gloss: to devote oneself; to work diligently

definitions.gloss: to devote oneself; to work diligently; to strive
definitions.explanation: To dedicate oneself wholeheartedly to study, training, or self-improvement. Originally a Buddhist term meaning ascetic practice.

examples.japanese: これからも{精進|しょうじん}します。
examples.english: I will continue to work hard.

examples.japanese: {日々|ひび}{精進|しょうじん}して{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{磨|みが}いている。
examples.english: I'm honing my skills through daily dedication.

examples.japanese: {師匠|ししょう}の{教|おし}えを{胸|むね}に、{一層|いっそう}{精進|しょうじん}してまいります。
examples.english: With my master's teachings close to my heart, I will devote myself even more.

notes:
USAGE:
A humble, formal expression often used in speeches, interviews, and formal declarations of commitment. Athletes, craftspeople, and public figures commonly use this word when pledging continued effort.

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally a Buddhist term ({精進|しょうじん}) meaning ascetic self-discipline, including abstaining from meat. The meaning broadened to general diligent effort.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日々|ひび}{精進|しょうじん}する (to devote oneself daily)
- {一層|いっそう}{精進|しょうじん}する (to strive even harder)
- {精進|しょうじん}{料理|りょうり} (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine)

GRAMMAR:
Suru-verb. Intransitive.
